page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.24xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz, the system features 48 physical cores supporting simultaneous multithreading for a total of 96 virtual CPUs. It incorporates 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided by bundled NVMe SSD volumes totaling 3,800 GB. Network capacity is anchored at a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct trade-off between single-core and multi-threaded scaling. Single-core performance evaluated via stress-ng falls in the bottom 10%, and Geekbench single-core reaches a score of 1314.0. However, multi-core workload results show strong capabilities across instruction-heavy tasks. The PassMark CPU encryption benchmark registers in the top 10% with a score of 98,126.63, benefiting from integrated AES and SHA-NI cryptographic hardware instructions. PassMark overall CPU, extended instruction, physics, and database operations tests place in the top 25%. Cached memory read throughput achieves 4,476.03 GB/sec in small block testing.

The c5ad.24xlarge instance demonstrates strong efficiency for compute-heavy parallel tasks requiring high local I/O throughput. Geekbench tests highlight top 25% throughput in software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing. Redis performance is high, executing 80.73 million SET operations per second. However, large model LLM text generation remains low due to memory capacity and lack of hardware GPU acceleration. This instance is best suited for high-density database deployments, build farm software compilation, image processing pipelines, and cryptographic processing where local NVMe storage and multi-core AMD EPYC density maximize hardware throughput per resource unit.
description: Amazon Web Services c5ad.24xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance powered by a 48-core AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz with simultaneous multithreading to deliver 96 vCPUs. Equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM and 3,800 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage, it offers a 2:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio alongside 20 Gbps baseline networking on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Benchmarks indicate top-tier performance in cryptographic encryption supported by AES and SHA hardware extensions, alongside top 25% results in software compilation, database operations, and Redis throughput at 80.73 million operations per second. While single-core speeds fall into lower benchmark tiers, multi-core parallel performance is robust. The bundled high-capacity local NVMe storage makes this instance effective for build farms, database management, and dense batch data processing.
